Carol Jessen is a San Francisco-based artist who studied at the Academy of Art in San Francisco and spent a year in Kyoto, Japan, where she studied Japanese woodblock printing with Toshi Yoshida. Her primary mediums are oil painting, pastel, and various forms of printmaking and collage.

Two of her woodblock prints are held in the permanent collection of the Cleveland Art Museum, and her work is also in the New York Public Library. Hunters Point Shipyard — the once-abandoned naval shipyard on San Francisco Bay — is now one of the largest artist communities in the United States, where Jessen has maintained her studio since 1988.

Acquired directly from the artist during Open Studios — an annual event where the public walks through working artists’ studios and buys directly from the source.
